en: Of the person seen by God,
The fortune of the sun was cut away,
He was a champion drawn toward the steppe,
Every living creature stood bewildered,
Those dear souls were no more,
Escaping torment upon the plain,
He was a champion most deeply mourned,
He entered the steppe and grieved,
Karagul upon the iron seat,
His restraining hand was torn away,
Finding no water in the desert-like waste,
The blue world became narrow,
How much water flowed through the ravine,
Longing only to see him once.
Rousing the people to the task,
Lamenting among a single people,
All were bound by their failing strength,
Every torment was endured,
It fell upon the heroes,
Their horses cropped no grass from the steppe,
The broad world became narrow,
No vision came to us,
Like snow upon black stone,
When the gray-maned heroes drank kumis,
Entering once, they lamented without asking,
Letting the hammer cover their heads,
They walked onward and away,
Forgetting the entire world,
They traveled on through the passing hour,
Their souls scorched like tobacco,
Their whole bodies were battered,
Shattering and scattering like meal,
Their pure hearts turned to bone,
Blood poured from the heroes,
The broad world closed in,
They appeared diminished and confined,
There was no resting place and no shelter,
Leading their souls toward death,
Burning for the people, without fear,
Wretched from exhaustion,
Tears the size of a child’s fist fell from their eyes,
Their migration faded as they cut through mountains,
A thousand chargers carved out the road,
The false world became narrow,
Their strength exhausted, they became wretched,
Lamenting beneath hostility,
Finding no comfortable land,
With no contentment filling their eyes,
Unable to attain what they longed for,
Their souls endured days of humiliation,
Suffering like a soul scorched to smoke,
A cartload burdened both shoulders,
They traveled onward in sorrow.
Calamity and hardship followed behind,
They traveled onward enduring it,
In grievous torment and hardship,
They continued on their way.
The children of men among the beasts,
How many bands rose from the earth,
Traveling onward through torment,
Bowing their heads in many lands,
They traveled onward from every side,
Made blue like an extraordinary soul,
Making it a land where none had been born,
Their fortune broken as blood was sought,
Let us reach the long span of their journey,
They went onward beside the waters,
Enduring the torment dealt by fists,
They traveled onward, withered and ruined.
Beyond them lay a broad valley with four branches,
When they came to that valley,
A great river valley lay there,
Swelling beneath the haze,
Blinding the eyes with its force,
A world of ease spread there,
Human eyes were captivated,
There was beauty in that valley,
It was land with snow upon its face,
It was deserted, with no living soul,
Its springs burst from cleft rock,
Its nightingales sang skillfully,
When the skillful nightingale sang mournfully,
A thousand eagles lived there,
Along the flank of that valley
There were patterned cliffs of every kind,
There were two kinds of apple and dates,
There were apricots and every kind of apple,
There was fruit lovely enough to draw the evil eye,
And there was wondrous land,
There were plane trees in dense stands,
There were towers touching the sky,
There were marvelous springs to behold.
Souls upon the hillside,
Every kind of person went there,
A land where people lay upon the earth,
A land where champions went seeking wonder,
Countless stallions gathered together,
Lying uncounted in Saidak,
Horses lay in the desert,
The Kyrgyz in barren China,
Bringing them down upon a mound like an ear,
It was a land hostile to the brave,
Men like bulls, men like mountains,
There were people who slaughtered them,
There was fame for shooting a tiger,
It was Zainap's rich speech,
There was strength that could wrestle a lion,
There were six untouched and unworn,
There was one called Sword-Swift,
There was prey for whoever had eyes,
How many champions lay there,
Taking the words of the bones upon his tongue,
Dividing every tribe,
Naming the horse, he descended contented,
Rejoicing in the gathering feast,
A deed that burned the grieving heart,
How could it ever leave my thoughts?
It was a land firm as the earth,
Its spirit was resolute,
The sands where they placed their trace,
What the tribe stood hearing,
Its birds faced toward China,
What was heard like a multitude,
There was a tongue born in the forest,
Each one possessed every wonder,
Awakening the many people,
Was it a land where none would settle?
The sun-bird of the silver eye,
Was it a land where nothing could be?
Hero Kenen, foremost upon Koktoo,
Was it a land that remained so?
A favorable city had been settled there.
It was a place from which one must depart.
You sons of the present age,
It was a land one had to cross.
They named it for deer and maral.
If you build it without ruin, set it straight.
They named it for argali and wild ram.
They truly raised them for spectacle.
They brought the wandering soul to rest.
They made a spectacle, sons of poison.
The giver struggled for his soul.
He stood exactly so.
Those were his ten dark cattle.
He was a bare and righteous soul.
The speaker struck the standing bond.
Each man took a spear in hand.
What kind of soul stood in calamity?
He himself belonged to the hidden people.
His eye was like a hard Indian gem.
He looked like a beast that had swallowed fire.
He did not recognize the form of man.
One fist seized him, yet he did not yield.
He brought concealment upon many peoples.
Its splendor came from its lineage.
The argali came from the givers.
They would drive it down upon the kulan.
He descended alive from the mountain pass.
The three lions saw this.
The day of fortune spread out.
The three lions saw the horror.
You have strength, and I have strength.
There is a deserted people who pursue heroes.
A life held in trust faces doomsday.
He brought a man down into freedom.
Without death and without misery,
He fashioned a man without suffering.
If God showed his face,
There is joy, and there is an enemy.
There is an evil one who walks through the years.
There was sand that could bury their heads,
There were red sheep of every kind,
Driving the herd toward the red country,
The lion-hearted men endured constriction and hardship,
Loading burdens upon their backs like coal,
The giant wandered on, striking all before him,
The livestock moved as their souls desired,
Toward the Masin River rich in maral deer,
The heroes went onward as scouts,
There was no road for the migrating flock,
The lake dazzled and blinded the eyes,
The land disappeared beneath water,
There it lay fitted among the rocks,
This was where the desert came to its end,
They made their way toward the great river,
Now it cast down all three of them,
In a deep and heavy sleep,
Everything else vanished from awareness,
They drew harsh, sharp breaths,
The heroes beside the Masin River,
Such was the heroes’ strength,
Their kinswoman had become a guest,
At the edge of that river,
While the bitter peril stood before them,
Upon the twin reaches of the steppe,
Their stone-like heads drooped,
Their hearts were oppressed within them,
Unable to wake, they lay insensible,
Falling into hardship and grief,
Word was sent from the horde,
It reached the mother,
The orphaned child was delivered,
Traveling through homeland after homeland,
Wandering beneath the sun through the world,
The people’s souls were scorched like smoke,
They laid down those three.
Words received after descending into the hollow,
The sun took its appointed season,
When the sixth day was fulfilled,
The time arrived and became day,
His land paled beneath the sun,
The dawn shielded itself and faded,
A star rose from the earth,
Life arose from the four directions,
He became a champion with a wolf's mane,
When the frost faded and he arrived,
The hero Kulan and the two champions,
Zhelzhetpes, keeper of the true secret,
The sovereign of the warrior people,
See the eyes that came from the Kyrgyz,
There is a trace behind the winter camp,
Escaping from the wrathful one,
His weapon was a massive shield,
A wretched support—see it, my eyes,
The livestock of two mountain folds,
At its head stands the Kokor horde,
A living creature beyond the hollow,
Take the thing after enduring its torment,
Enough—this is the true champion,
He was Kokzhal beside the water,
At dawn's touch, beside the water,
Grieving in torment like hell,
His soul beyond was a leaden bullet,
These sorrowful bullets were many,
The day held torment; there were seven,
There is a strong coat; if he goes, it remains,
Within the work of the moonlike eye,
How much unrest there was,
The land was his elder brother's inheritance,
Among three wrathful souls,
How many came to that place,
There was a corner where an age might pass,
All I carried came from the soul.
Reciting verses of the Quran in turn,
Saying it opened the heart within the breast,
They were a poor and afflicted people,
Saying it opened a single brow,
Ordaining days of life,
Saying it opened a troubled heart,
They laid down the great gun,
The poor men called the azan from afar,
Pleading with the Creator,
Beside the river within reach,
At the plane tree that propped up the sky,
Having it prepared in a stone cauldron,
Saying God would grant it now,
